newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece says ready to match any Turkish challenge.
newsitem.headline: Greece says ready to match any Turkish challenge.

text.p: Greece said it would meet any attempt by neighbouring Turkey to change the status quo in the Aegean by an equal show of force on both a military and a political level.

"If Turkey provokes a new incident, the Greek response will be, apart from military, also political," Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos said in a speech on national defence policy in the northern port city of Salonika late on Friday.
"This response will maximise the cost for Ankara, be proportionate to the seriousness of the provocation and in the framework of implementing international agreements," he said.
Tsohatzopoulos did not specify whether Greece would go ahead with extending its territorial waters to 12 nautical miles, which Turkey has said would be cause for war.

As a signatory to the international Law of the Sea convention, Greece has the right to extend its territorial waters from the current six to 12 miles. Turkey, which is not a signatory to the convention, has said this would make the Aegean a "Greek lake".

The defence minister said it was "pointless" to pressure Ankara to take its dispute over the Aegean islet of Imia, which brought the two countries to the brink of war last January, to the International Court at the Hague.
"Recourse to the Hague is pointless because Ankara's logic is devoid of any perspective for a lawful settlement of the issue. Its logic is to impose its views on Athens," he said.
Tsohatzopoulos described Turkey as the "number one threat to Greece" saying Ankara would not balk at using force to create "the status quo it desires in the Aegean".
Territorial rights in the Aegean Sea are among a long list of grievances between the two NATO allies, who are also at odds over the divided island of Cyprus and minority rights in both countries.
